turns.text: I record every successful charge, but I never check whether the same order was already charged, so a repeated request becomes a fresh entry in the list of charges. That is a nasty little pileup: `processCharge` calls `authorizeAndCapture` and then `recordCharge` with a brand-new `chargeId` every time, with no idempotency key (a unique ID that makes a repeated request safe to repeat). [payments/processor.ts:29-49] [payments/ledger.ts:11-19]

I am the one retrying the payment on timeout, and that is the damn second punch. `checkout` retries `requestCharge` when `UpstreamTimeoutError` hits, but it sends only `order_id`, amount, currency, and `payment_method_id`; there is no idempotency key, so a timed-out first charge can still succeed and the retry charges again. [orders/checkout.ts:20-30] [orders/checkout.ts:43-58]

I cut the request off after `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000`, while payments says its typical processing time is about 2400ms and p99 is 4s. That means I can throw a timeout while the card network is still finishing, which is a lovely shitshow when the caller retries the same charge. [gateway/config.ts:15-16] [gateway/proxy.ts:25-53]

I’m not the first domino, but I am the place where the duplicate money lands. The log shows the same order charged twice with two different `chargeId` values, `ord_8f3k2b61` at 14:02:11 and again at 14:02:13, so the downstream retry path is real, not imaginary bullshit. [payments/logs/sample-charges.log:6-7]

I did exactly what my code says: on timeout I try again once, because someone bolted on a retry to fix flaky checkouts. With a 2000ms gateway cutoff and payments taking ~2400ms on average, that retry is a damn duplicate generator unless the charge request is made safe to repeat. [orders/checkout.ts:44-57]

I am not inventing extra charges; I am exposing a timing bug by failing faster than the payment service usually finishes. The real fix is to make the charge request safe to repeat, because a longer timeout alone just hides the shit under the rug. [gateway/proxy.ts:25-29]

verdict.rootCause: The gateway times out after 2000ms, but the payment call usually takes about 2400ms, so the first charge can still finish after the gateway has already given up. Orders then retries that same charge without an idempotency key (a unique ID that makes a repeated request safe to repeat), so the payment service creates a second successful charge. Payments also lacks duplicate detection, so it accepts both requests and records both charges.
verdict.judgeLine: The code timed out first and retried second, which is a classic little fuck-up in payment systems.
